newsitem.title: USA: Chubb to sell life insurance unit to Jefferson-Pilot.
newsitem.headline: Chubb to sell life insurance unit to Jefferson-Pilot.

text.p: Chubb Corp. has a definitive agreement to sell Chubb Life Insurance Co. of America to Jefferson-Pilot Corp. for $875 million in cash, the companies said Monday.
The combined companies will have more than 25,000 sales representatives, almost two million customers, and more than $160 billion of life insurance in force.

Jefferson-Pilot, based in Greensboro, N.C., said the acquisition is a step in its plan to grow faster than its competitors and become one of the largest providers in each of its target product and geographic markets.

"With the purchase of Chubb Life, our combined companies will rank in the top 15 of life insurance companies nationwide based on total life premium income," said Jefferson-Pilot President and Chief Executive David Stonecipher.
"Annual life sales will be approximately $200 million, ranking us in the top 10 life insurance companies in the United States for life sales."
In a separate statement, Chubb said the Warren, N.J.-based company intends to use a substantial portion of the proceeds of the sale to buy back its own stock.

Chubb Chairman and Chief Executive Dean O'Hare said the management of Chubb Life has "done a terrific job turning the company around in the last two years." But the trend of consolidation in life insurance has created an industry in which scale is increasingly important, he added.

Chubb Life and its subsidiaries offer a broad range of individual life insurance products and are leading providers of variable universal life products. They have assets of nearly $5 billion and distribute their products through an independent network that includes more than 1,300 general agents and 9,000 agents.

Jefferson-Pilot is one of the nation's largest shareholder-owned life insurance companies. Its Jefferson-Pilot Communications Co. owns and operates three network affiliated television stations, 17 radio stations and a sports production company.

Chubb is also in final negotiations to sell 80 percent of of its real estate business, Bellemead Development Corp., to either Dallas' Patriot American Hospitality Inc. and Boston's Beacon Properties Corp., for about $1 billion, including debt, the New York Times reported Monday.
The report said it is uncertain which company will win the deal for Chubb's real estate unit.
Chubb's stock rose 87.5 cents to $58.625, while Jefferson-Pilot edged down 37.5 cents to $57.25 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
